name: devtools-dock
description: Phase C2: Cmd+Opt+I on a chromeless window opens DevTools DOCKED into the inspected tab's pane rather than in a separate window. Atrium windows have no BrowserView, so stock Chromium's docking (DevtoolsUIController) does not apply - AtriumBrowserWindow::UpdateDockedDevtoolsForPane re-implements it per pane, and that function's dock-state VLOG is the assertion source. The window-count assertion is the other half of 'docked': a DETACHED DevTools would add an AXStandardWindow, so the count staying at its baseline is what distinguishes docked from undocked. Uses the presenter-startup spaces fixture because it starts on a space with exactly one real tab, which is all a dock needs (the pane's WebContents exists whether or not the page actually loaded in the VM).

actions.note: let the space and its single tab render
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot; without this the keystroke lands in Finder (traffic-routing learned this the hard way)
open DevTools on the active tab
DevTools frontend is a full WebContents load - generous on purpose, the dock VLOG only fires once UpdateDockedDevtoolsForPane runs with a non-null GetInTabWebContents

assertions.label: devtools-docked
assertions.note: The pane resolved a docked DevTools WebContents - the sole writer of this state
still ONE standard window: a detached DevTools would add a second, so this is what proves 'docked' rather than merely 'opened'
